patterns.source: project/paper.txt Table 3 vs. Table 4 (SWE-Bench Lite, CodeActAgent v1.8, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 cell)
patterns.rhetorical_purpose: n/a -- an extraction/production defect, not an authorial rhetorical choice
move_sequence: a redundant summary table (Table 3) restates numbers already given in a dedicated table (Table 4)
one restated value (6.3) silently disagrees with the dedicated table's value for the identical cell (7.0)
patterns.evidence_placement: the disagreement sits in two different tables rather than being visibly flagged anywhere
patterns.signature: a 'curated' redundant summary table that duplicates, and in one cell contradicts, a dedicated results table
patterns.reader_effect: a careful reader who checks both tables loses confidence in exactly which number is authoritative
patterns.repair_principle: treat the dedicated, internally cross-validated table as authoritative and record the redundant table's conflicting cell as superseded, rather than silently picking one value or averaging them (applied in this run: E004/E001, state.json AR003)

patterns.source: project/paper.txt Table 1 (framework comparison) and Table 7 (extended GPQA results)
move_sequence: a multi-column comparison table's header/row labels survive text extraction
the table's actual cell values (check-marks, or a large numeric block) do not survive, or cannot be reliably realigned to their rows/columns
patterns.evidence_placement: the table appears intact until someone tries to read a specific cell
patterns.signature: a wide comparison table whose cell values are structurally absent or unrecoverable from extracted text
patterns.reader_effect: a reader (or a downstream writer relying on the extraction) could be tempted to fill in plausible-looking values for missing cells
patterns.repair_principle: mark the table's evidence item status=unverifiable/incomplete and do not use it to support any specific comparative claim (applied in this run: E043, E044; hard rule against creative gap-filling)

note: Scoped down per state.json accepted_risk AR005 (no web access; no external exemplar corpus available).
